plan.rationale: The torch collector already ran and fully attributed the trace (coverage.json: cuda_kernels=88, associated_kernels=88, unassociated=0, ambiguous_forward_sequences=0, autograd_ranges=0), so no attribution, overlap, or graph-tracing question remains to justify nsys. The frozen objective is latency_ms for one complete offline batch=32 forward between two torch.cuda.synchronize() calls on a single GPU with no distributed backend, so nccl_tuning, collective_calibration, and all communication/bucket dimensions are not applicable (observations.json marks communication 'not_applicable: single-device task'), and device_telemetry is declined because its device-wide PCIe/utilization/memory readings have native sampling windows that cannot attribute a single short forward, the model and pixels are already GPU-resident, and peak_allocated_bytes is recorded by the source harness. candidate_diagnostics and binding_cost are inapplicable before any candidate exists. The two open diagnostic questions for reducing this latency are (1) whether the GPU is starved inside the measured region, addressed by execution_timeline via per-device CUDA intervals, CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization events, and clock alignment bounds (used only as bounds; GPU readiness/consumer completion may stay unknown), and (2) how much host dispatch and binding cost contributes, addressed by python_runtime's warmed cProfile call trace with the explicit caveat that it perturbs execution and its times are not clean performance scores or GPU durations. Host-side prerequisites were confirmed in the measured worker's interpreter (/root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv/bin/python: 3.12.4, torch 2.13.0+cu129, cProfile available).
